# On-demand delivery workers’ minimum pay rates and other standards start today
On-demand delivery workers have new minimum standards that start today, including minimum pay rates based on an hourly rate of at least $31.30, as the first ever Fair Work Commission Minimum Standards Order takes effect.

This includes a requirement for digital labour platform operators to make a top-up payment if an employee-like worker's earnings for an earnings period (which can be up to 21 days) fall below the applicable minimum earnings floor.

The earnings floor is calculated by multiplying the worker's total hours of engaged time by the relevant minimum hourly rates set by the order, which are:

- $31.30 for food delivery gig workers with no vehicle, on pedal-powered or electric bicycles, or on electric scooters
- $31.50 for those on motorcycles or combustion scooters
- $32 if they use a car or van (up to 1 tonne capacity).

These minimum rates are subject to future adjustment, including through annual wage review increases.

Namely, if they want to take time away from an app, they can choose not to accept engagements – and during this time, won’t be paid.

We pay our respects to them, their Cultures, and Elders past and present.
